body_html:
Why the order matters

An expression with more than one operation could give different answers if people worked in a different order. So everyone uses the same order of operations. In Ontario classrooms it is remembered as BEDMAS.

StepDo thisExample
1Brackets(25 + 15) × 3 = 40 × 3 = 120
2Exponents3 + 2³ = 3 + 8 = 11
3÷ and ×, as equals, from left to right12 ÷ 2 × 3 = 6 × 3 = 18
4+ and −, as equals, from left to right20 − 8 + 3 = 12 + 3 = 15

D and M are a team, and so are A and S

BEDMAS lists D before M, but division does not always come first. ÷ and × have the same rank, so do whichever comes first from the left. The same is true for + and −.

Brackets and an exponent

Evaluate (5 + 3)² − 10.

(5 + 3)² − 10 = 8² − 10 = 64 − 10 = 54.

Answer: 54

An exponent means repeated multiplication: 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, not 2 × 3 = 6. Powers of 10 help with large numbers: 4 × 10⁵ = 400 000.

Decimals and fractions

The order is the same with decimals and fractions. Only the arithmetic at each step changes.

Decimals

Evaluate 2.5 + 1.5 × 4.

2.5 + 1.5 × 4 = 2.5 + 6 = 8.5. Not 16: that adds first.

Answer: 8.5

Fractions

Evaluate 34 + 12 × 3.

34 + 12 × 3 = 34 + 1 12 = 2 14. Not 3 34: that adds first.

Answer: 2 14

Properties make mental math faster

The distributive property lets you split a number into friendly parts: a × (b + c) = a × b + a × c. Multiply both parts.

The commutative and associative properties let you change the order and the grouping of a product: 25 × 37 × 4 = 25 × 4 × 37 = 100 × 37 = 3700.

Word problems as one expression

Write the whole problem as one expression, then use BEDMAS. Use brackets when a sum must be found before you multiply or divide.

Change from $20

Mei buys 3 hot chocolates at $3.75 each and pays with a $20 bill. How much change does she get?

One expression: 20 − 3 × 3.75 = 20 − 11.25 = 8.75.

Answer: $8.75

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
3 + 4 × 2 = 7 × 2 = 14Multiply first: 3 + 8 = 11
12 ÷ 2 × 3 = 12 ÷ 6 = 2÷ and × are equals: left to right, 6 × 3 = 18
20 − 8 + 3 = 20 − 11 = 9+ and − are equals: left to right, 12 + 3 = 15
2³ = 6An exponent means repeated multiplication: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8
6 × 98 = 600 − 2 = 598Multiply both parts: 600 − 12 = 588

faq.q: What is BEDMAS in Grade 7 math?
faq.a: BEDMAS is the order of operations used in Ontario: Brackets, Exponents, Division and Multiplication (left to right), then Addition and Subtraction (left to right). For example, 3 + 4 × 2 = 3 + 8 = 11, not 14.

faq.q: Is BEDMAS the same as PEMDAS and BODMAS?
faq.a: Yes. PEMDAS (used in the US) and BODMAS (used in the UK) give the same order with different words. In all of them, × and ÷ have the same rank and so do + and −, so 12 ÷ 2 × 3 = 18.

faq.q: Where is order of operations in the Ontario Grade 7 math curriculum?
faq.a: It is in the Number strand, expectation B2.1: students use the properties and order of operations to solve problems with whole numbers, decimals, fractions, ratios, rates and percents, including multi-step problems.

faq.q: How does the distributive property help with mental math?
faq.a: It lets you split a number into friendly parts and multiply each part. For example, 7 × 98 = 7 × 100 − 7 × 2 = 700 − 14 = 686.

sets.title: Multi-step word problems in one expression

items.q: In a class quiz game, a correct answer earns 4 points and a wrong answer loses 2 points. Arjun gets 8 correct and 5 wrong. What is his score?
items.e: One expression: 8 × 4 − 5 × 2. 8 × 4 − 5 × 2 = 32 − 5 × 2 = 32 − 10 = 22, so 22 points. Not 54 points: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not −16 points: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing. Not 42 points: that adds the points for wrong answers.

items.q: Jayden buys 3 rolls of hockey tape at $4.25 each and a puck for $2.50. Which expression gives the total cost?
items.e: 3 × 4.25 + 2.5 = 12.75 + 2.5 = 15.25. So the total is $15.25. 3 × (4.25 + 2.5) would mean 3 pucks. The other two multiply the wrong numbers.

items.q: A ringette team of 15 players has 5 cases of 24 water bottles. They keep 30 bottles for the next game and share the rest equally among the players. How many bottles does each player get?
items.e: One expression: (5 × 24 − 30) ÷ 15. (5 × 24 − 30) ÷ 15 = (120 − 30) ÷ 15 = 90 ÷ 15 = 6, so 6 bottles. Not 118 bottles: that comes from ignoring the brackets. Not 90 bottles: that forgets to share among the players. Not 10 bottles: that adds the 30 bottles instead of taking them away.

items.q: A Grade 7 class of 27 students visits the Royal Ontario Museum. Each ticket costs $14, and the bus costs $325. What is the total cost?
items.e: One expression: 27 × 14 + 325. 27 × 14 + 325 = 378 + 325 = 703, so $703. Not $9153: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing. Not $366: that adds all the numbers. Not $339: that pays for only one student.

items.q: Priya earns $15 an hour babysitting. She works 3 hours on Friday and 4 hours on Saturday. Which expression gives her total pay?
items.e: 15 × (3 + 4) = 15 × 7 = 105. So she earns $105. Without the brackets, 15 × 3 + 4 adds only $4 for Saturday.

items.q: At 4:00 p.m. the temperature in Sudbury is 3°C. It drops 2°C every hour for 4 hours. Which expression gives the new temperature?
items.e: 3 − 4 × 2 = 3 − 8 = −5. So the new temperature is −5°C. (3 − 4) × 2 subtracts before multiplying. 4 × 2 − 3 subtracts in the wrong order and gives 5°C.

items.q: A hockey stick costs $120. It is on sale for 25% off. Ethan also buys a roll of tape for $6. How much does he pay before tax?
items.e: One expression: 120 − 0.25 × 120 + 6. 120 − 0.25 × 120 + 6 = 120 − 30 + 6 = 90 + 6 = 96, so $96. Not $36: that pays only the $30 discount plus the tape, not the sale price. Not $101: that takes off $25 instead of 25%. Not $90: that stops one step too early.

items.q: A school has 640 students. 15% walk to school and 25% take the bus. The rest come by car. How many students come by car?
items.e: One expression: 640 − (0.15 + 0.25) × 640. 640 − (0.15 + 0.25) × 640 = 640 − 0.4 × 640 = 640 − 256 = 384, so 384 students. Not 256 students: that finds the students who walk or take the bus. Not 544 students: that subtracts only the students who walk. Not 600 students: that subtracts 40 instead of 40%.

items.q: A car uses 7.5 L of gas for every 100 km. A family drives 450 km from Toronto to Ottawa. How much gas does the car use?
items.e: One expression: 450 ÷ 100 × 7.5. 450 ÷ 100 × 7.5 = 4.5 × 7.5 = 33.75, so 33.75 L. Not 0.6 L: that comes from multiplying before dividing, but × and ÷ have the same rank, so work left to right. Not 60 L: that divides by the rate. Not 4.5 L: that stops one step too early.

items.q: At a sugar bush, maple syrup costs $12 for a small bottle and $21 for a large jug. Chloe buys 3 bottles and 2 jugs. She pays with a $100 bill. How much change does she get?
items.e: One expression: 100 − (3 × 12 + 2 × 21). 100 − (3 × 12 + 2 × 21) = 100 − (36 + 2 × 21) = 100 − (36 + 42) = 100 − 78 = 22, so $22. Not $106: that comes from ignoring the brackets. Not $78: that forgets to subtract from $100. Not $43: that pays for only one jug.

items.q: A diver in Georgian Bay is at −12 m (12 m below the surface). She rises 3 m two times, then sinks 7 m. Where is she now?
items.e: One expression: (−12) + 2 × 3 − 7. (−12) + 2 × 3 − 7 = (−12) + 6 − 7 = (−6) − 7 = −13, so −13 m. Not −37 m: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not 11 m: that forgets that −12 m is below the surface. Not −25 m: that subtracts the rises instead of adding them.

items.q: In a class of 30 students, the ratio of students who walk to school to students who take the bus is 2 : 3. How many students take the bus?
items.e: One expression: 30 ÷ (2 + 3) × 3. 30 ÷ (2 + 3) × 3 = 30 ÷ 5 × 3 = 6 × 3 = 18, so 18 students. Not 24 students: that comes from ignoring the brackets. Not 12 students: that finds the students who walk. Not 10 students: that divides by 3 instead of by the 5 parts.

items.q: At the skating rink, Mei buys 3 hot chocolates at $3.75 each. She pays with a $20 bill. How much change does she get?
items.e: One expression: 20 − 3 × 3.75. 20 − 3 × 3.75 = 20 − 11.25 = 8.75, so $8.75. Not $63.75: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not $16.25: that pays for only one hot chocolate. Not $11.25: that stops one step too early.

items.q: A bus fare is $2.75. Olivia takes 2 bus rides a day for 5 school days. She starts with $40 on her transit card. How much is left at the end of the week?
items.e: One expression: 40 − 2 × 5 × 2.75. 40 − 2 × 5 × 2.75 = 40 − 10 × 2.75 = 40 − 27.5 = 12.5, so $12.50. Not $522.50: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not $26.25: that counts only one ride a day. Not $37.25: that counts only one ride.

items.q: Maya has 12 m of ribbon. She uses 34 of it for a project, then buys 5 m more. How much ribbon does she have now?
items.e: One expression: 12 − 34 × 12 + 5. 12 − 34 × 12 + 5 = 12 − 9 + 5 = 3 + 5 = 8, so 8 m. Not 140 m: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not 14 m: that adds to the part she used, not the part left. Not 3 m: that stops one step too early.

items.q: A canoe rental at a cottage costs $15 for the first hour and $9 for each extra hour. Liam rents a canoe for 4 hours. How much does he pay?
items.e: One expression: 15 + 3 × 9. 15 + 3 × 9 = 15 + 27 = 42, so $42. Not $162: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not $51: that charges the first hour twice. Not $36: that uses $9 for every hour.

items.q: Hana’s scores on four math quizzes are 18, 15, 20 and 17. What is her mean score?
items.e: One expression: (18 + 15 + 20 + 17) ÷ 4. (18 + 15 + 20 + 17) ÷ 4 = (33 + 20 + 17) ÷ 4 = (53 + 17) ÷ 4 = 70 ÷ 4 = 17.5, so 17.5 points. Not 57.25 points: that comes from ignoring the brackets. Not 280 points: that multiplies instead of dividing. Not 70 points: that stops one step too early.

items.q: At the Terry Fox Run, Noah runs 3 laps of a 1.6 km loop and then 0.8 km to the finish line. How far does he run in all?
items.e: One expression: 3 × 1.6 + 0.8. 3 × 1.6 + 0.8 = 4.8 + 0.8 = 5.6, so 5.6 km. Not 7.2 km: that comes from adding or subtracting before multiplying or dividing. Not 2.4 km: that counts only one lap. Not 4.8 km: that stops one step too early.

items.q: A hockey team plays 6 games. It scores 2 goals in each of 4 games and 5 goals in each of the other 2 games. What is the mean number of goals per game?
items.e: One expression: (4 × 2 + 2 × 5) ÷ 6. (4 × 2 + 2 × 5) ÷ 6 = (8 + 2 × 5) ÷ 6 = (8 + 10) ÷ 6 = 18 ÷ 6 = 3, so 3 goals. Not 9 goals: that divides by the 2 kinds of game, not the 6 games. Not 3.5 goals: that finds the mean of 2 and 5, not of the 6 games. Not 18 goals: that stops one step too early.

items.q: At 7:00 a.m. the temperature in Thunder Bay is −11°C. It rises 2°C every hour for 5 hours. What is the temperature at noon?
items.e: One expression: (−11) + 2 × 5. (−11) + 2 × 5 = (−11) + 10 = −1, so −1°C. Not −45°C: that comes from working left to right without doing × and ÷ first. Not 10°C: that forgets the starting temperature. Not 21°C: that drops the minus sign on −11.
